intended_object: The vertical pasting, in a bicategory, of a square β : g ≫ l₃ ⟶ l₂ ≫ h with a 2-cell α : l₂ ⟶ l₁ between the left adjoints (a "conjugate square"). The result is the square g ≫ l₃ ⟶ l₁ ≫ h. This is read off the docstring and from how the companion theorem `conjugateEquiv_mateEquiv_vcomp` uses it.
explanation:
The body is `β ≫ α ▷ h`: first apply β, then whisker α on the right by h. The types line up, and this is exactly the pasting of the two 2-cells along their shared edge l₂. It is the standard composite that appears in mate calculus. The adjunctions adj₁, adj₂ and adj₃ are section variables that the body does not mention, so they are not arguments of the definition. That is correct, because the pasting does not depend on them. The adjunctions only matter in the theorem stating that mates are compatible with this composition.

The definition is stated for an arbitrary bicategory, which is the natural generality for mate calculus. It is not specialised to `Cat`. I searched Mathlib and found no other declaration with this name, so there is no broader counterpart.

The definition is mainly a helper for stating `conjugateEquiv_mateEquiv_vcomp`. Still, it captures a genuine and correctly stated pasting operation on 2-cells, so I judge it faithful.
